newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures firm more late, end stronger.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures firm more late, end stronger.

text.p: U.S. debt futures firmed again late to end moderately higher and hugging day's peaks.

September Treasury bond futures nosed up to session highs near the close, surpassing Monday's high at 110-01/32 that had capped the market and made some brokers look for more uninspired range-trading until Friday's May U.S. jobs data.
The final move higher occurred when a couple of dealers and a big local bought, possibly looking for stops, as turnover finally picked up again, brokers said.
They said the market already had absorbed the 0.5-percent rise in weekly Redbook retail sales with little fanfare.
"That was in for half an hour before (the rise)," said a T-bond futures floor broker of the weekly retail sales report.

The close above 110-01/32 in September T-bonds was viewed as technically supportive but still left brokers uncertain about the contract's ability to trudge much higher soon, especially into Friday's data.
"It wasn't a weak close but it still isn't outside the trading range," said a second T-bond futures broker.
He said the contract still faced the May 16 high at 110-04/32 as well as the spike high of 110-09/32 from May 13.
"I would sell it up here," he added.

"It's hard to get an attitude about this market because there have been so many false starts in the last month," said another T-bond futures floor broker, adding that he wanted to avoid getting bullish again too quickly.

Futures showed little response to afternoon comments by Treasury secretary Robert Rubin on banking and financial reform and by deputy Treasury secretary Lawrence Summers on the bright outlook for the U.S economy.
Nor did futures move when San Francisco Federal Reserve Bank president Robert Parry said the key to money policy is whether the economy slows to a sustainable growth rate.
